name: Bhujangasana (Cobra pose)
noEquipmentAlternative: Sphinx pose on forearms on a carpet, or a standing wall chest opener
musclesSecondary: stretched: rectus abdominis, pectoralis major, hip flexors

setupSteps: Lay the mat on a flat, non-slip floor (a rug on tiles can slide; put the mat against a wall or sofa end if needed).
Lie face down. Legs straight behind you, feet hip-width or together, tops of the feet flat on the mat (toes pointing back, not curled under, which keeps the thighs relaxed).
Forehead on the mat. A folded towel under the forehead or hips is fine if the floor is hard.

Place the palms flat on the mat beside the lower ribs, fingertips roughly level with the chest. Beginner default: hands slightly ahead of the shoulders, elbows bent and tucked in towards the body (a classic description puts the hands in front of the shoulders to spare the back). Elbows point backward, not out to the sides.
Legs: press the tops of the thighs and the pubic bone into the floor and gently tuck the tailbone down. Do not clench the buttocks hard.
Check wrists: if wrists ache in this position, rest on the forearms (sphinx) instead.
Camera: phone on the floor or a low stool, side-on, 2–2.5 m away (see section 11).

steps.title: Lie down and settle
steps.action: lie face down, forehead on the mat, arms bent with palms beside the chest.
steps.feel: belly, chest and hips resting on the mat.
steps.visualCheck: side view, the body in one long line; front view, elbows close to the ribs.

steps.title: Set the legs and hips
steps.action: press the tops of the thighs, hip bones and feet into the floor.
steps.feel: a gentle firmness in the thighs and buttocks, not a clench.
steps.visualCheck: side view, hips and thighs touching the mat.

steps.title: Look down, then lengthen the neck
steps.action: slide the chin slightly in and stretch the back of the neck long.
steps.feel: the back of the neck long, shoulders away from the ears.
steps.visualCheck: side view, ear, shoulder and spine in one line, not looking up.

steps.title: Lift the head and chest using the back muscles (baby cobra)
steps.action: on a slow breath in, peel the head, then the shoulders and upper chest off the mat. The hands stay on the floor with light pressure only; imagine sliding the hands slightly back toward the feet without moving them.
steps.feel: a working feeling along the spine between and below the shoulder blades, not a squeeze at the low back.
steps.visualCheck: side view, lower ribs and the navel still on the mat or hovering about 3 cm (est.) at most; the chest has risen only a hand's width (est.).

steps.title: Roll the shoulders back and down
steps.action: draw the shoulder blades gently toward each other and slightly down, lifting the breastbone forward.
steps.feel: chest opening, shoulders away from the ears.
steps.visualCheck: front view, shoulders level and low, elbows still bent and by the ribs.

steps.title: Hold
steps.action: stay at a comfortable height; keep the thighs and pelvis down and the neck long.
steps.feel: mild muscle effort in the back and a gentle stretch across the front of the chest and belly. Overall effort is light: 3–4/10 on the ACSM 0–10 perceived-exertion scale (= Borg 9–11 on the 6–20 scale).
steps.breathing: normal, easy breathing (the NIOS manual says breathe normally at the final position); never hold the breath.
steps.tempo: 15–30 seconds (about 3–5 slow breaths, est.); see section 7.
steps.visualCheck: side view, a smooth gentle arch in the upper back; no sharp fold in the low back.

steps.title: Optional: deepen to full cobra
steps.action: only if the back is comfortable, press lightly into the hands and straighten the arms a little (stop before the elbows lock) while the pelvis and thighs stay down. Straight arms are not required; how far the arms straighten depends on flexibility.
steps.feel: a deeper stretch in the front of the body, the work spread over the whole back; no pinch in the low back.
steps.breathing: breathe in while rising a little, then normal.
steps.tempo: 3 seconds, then hold up to 15 seconds (est.).
steps.visualCheck: side view, hips on the mat, the arch spread through the spine, shoulders not up by the ears.

steps.title: Lower down slowly
steps.action: breathe out and slowly lower chest, shoulders and head in the reverse order.
steps.visualCheck: side view, controlled descent, no dropping.

steps.title: Rest
steps.action: turn the head to one side, rest the cheek on the stacked hands, or sit back into Balasana (Child's Pose, Yoga & Stretch 8) for a few breaths to unload the back.
steps.feel: lower back soft; breathing returns to normal.

steps.title: Repeat, then get up safely
steps.action: do 3 rounds (section 7), then press into the hands, push back into Child's Pose or onto all fours, and stand slowly.
steps.visualCheck: no sudden sit-up from a flat back.

steps.part: Sphinx version (easiest; each step: action | feel | breath | tempo | visual check)
steps.title: Lie face down, then rest on the forearms with the elbows under the shoulders, forearms parallel and palms down | chest slightly lifted, back soft | breathe in | 4 s | side view, upper arms near vertical

steps.part: Sphinx version (easiest; each step: action | feel | breath | tempo | visual check)
steps.title: Press the forearms lightly into the floor and lengthen the neck | upper back gently working | breathe out | 3 s | ears over shoulders, not craning

steps.part: Sphinx version (easiest; each step: action | feel | breath | tempo | visual check)
steps.title: Hold and breathe | mild, steady stretch in the front of the trunk | slow breathing | 20–30 s (est.) | hips and thighs on the mat

steps.part: Sphinx version (easiest; each step: action | feel | breath | tempo | visual check)
steps.title: Lower down slowly | back lets go | breathe out | 4 s | controlled

commonMistakes.title: Pushing up with the arms and straightening the elbows too soon
commonMistakes.text: Pushing up with the arms and straightening the elbows too soon. The back muscles do nothing and the low back takes the load. Fix: keep the elbows bent, lift with the back, and use "light hands".

commonMistakes.title: Hips and thighs lifting off the floor (drifting toward Upward Dog)
commonMistakes.text: Hips and thighs lifting off the floor (drifting toward Upward Dog). Changes the pose, loads the wrists and low back. Fix: press the pubic bone and thighs down; if you cannot, lower the height (Cam Yoga, Yoga International).

commonMistakes.title: Throwing the head back and crunching the neck
commonMistakes.text: Throwing the head back and crunching the neck. Compresses the back of the neck. Fix: long neck, gaze down, lift as one piece with the chest.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears. Tightens the neck and shortens the chest. Fix: roll the shoulders back and down first.

commonMistakes.title: Clenching the buttocks and bending only at the low back
commonMistakes.text: Clenching the buttocks and bending only at the low back. A sharp fold at one spot. Fix: soften the glutes, lengthen the tailbone toward the heels, spread the arch through the upper back.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Raises tension and blood pressure. Fix: normal, easy breathing in the hold (NIOS manual).

commonMistakes.title: Going too high for a stiff back
commonMistakes.text: Going too high for a stiff back. Pain or pinching in the low back means the lift is too big. Fix: drop to sphinx or lower down and rest.

commonMistakes.title: Flared elbows or wrists bent hard
commonMistakes.text: Flared elbows or wrists bent hard. Strains the wrists and shoulders. Fix: elbows tucked, hands slightly ahead of the shoulders, or switch to forearms.

commonMistakes.title: Jumping to Upward Dog before cobra is steady
commonMistakes.text: Jumping to Upward Dog before cobra is steady. One teaching source calls this the most common cause of low-back and wrist strain in flow classes. Fix: master baby cobra for several weeks first.

safetyNotes: Lower back: an extension pose. Use baby cobra or sphinx only, avoid it with a recent lower-back injury, practise a slipped disc only under instruction, and stop if back pain increases. Some low back pain responds to extension and some gets worse; if leg pain or numbness starts, stop.
Wrist and elbow problems, carpal tunnel: use the sphinx (forearms) version.
Neck: keep the neck long; stop if there is neck pain or tingling in the arms.

Abdominal surgery, hernia, peptic ulcer: avoid or practise only under expert guidance (NIOS manual lists peptic ulcer, hernia, hypertension and hyperthyroidism under expert guidance; Bajaj Allianz and others say avoid after recent abdominal surgery).
Pregnancy: avoid lying face-down (pressure on the abdomen); use a standing or seated chest opener instead.
Asthma: do not practise during an attack.
Stop immediately if you feel: sharp or pinching low-back pain; pain, tingling or numbness down an arm or leg; neck pain; wrist pain; dizziness; stomach or incision pain; breathlessness.
Gym etiquette: use the stretching area or a mat out of walkways; wipe the mat after use.

Baby vs full cobra: bent-arm (baby, low) is gentler and strength-focused; straight-arm (full) is deeper. We teach baby cobra first and make full cobra an option (sources use the terms loosely).
Hold time and rounds: 15-30 s (Amala) and 3-5 rounds (NIOS); some guides ~10 s. We chose 3 rounds of 15 s for beginners.
Hand position: classic description (hands in front of the shoulders) vs under the shoulders or beside the ribs; we use slightly ahead of the shoulders with tucked elbows.
Cobra vs Upward Dog: cobra keeps pelvis and thighs down with bent elbows; Upward Dog lifts the thighs, straightens the arms and loads the wrists. We teach them as separate poses.
Hypertension and back-bends: NIOS says expert guidance; Art of Living says avoid back-bends. We chose "ask a doctor", baby cobra or sphinx only.
Osteoporosis: extension is generally favoured over flexion (UK consensus), but forced deep arches are not advised for spine fracture; we say modify.
Lower back pain: extension helps some and aggravates others; the pose-specific trial evidence is Not found.
Pregnancy: guidance concerns lying on the back; for lying face-down we follow the pose sources (avoid).
